Revenue / Subscription economics

Simplified gross-profit lifetime value (LTV)

An approximate lifetime gross-profit value per subscription customer using monthly revenue, gross margin, and monthly logo churn. This is an explicit steady-state model, not a prediction of every customer's actual lifetime value.

An approximate lifetime gross-profit value per subscription customer using monthly revenue, gross margin, and monthly logo churn. This is an explicit steady-state model, not a prediction of every customer's actual lifetime value.

currency / customer

How we use it

Use as an initial scenario alongside CAC. We can replace this approximation with observed cohort cash flows when sufficient customer history is available.

Transparent calculationMonthly average revenue per paying customer × gross-margin fraction ÷ monthly customer-churn fraction
monthly revenue per customer200
gross margin percent75
monthly customer churn percent5

200 × 0.75 ÷ 0.05 = 3,000 currency units of modeled lifetime gross profit.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Customer cohort and plan
  • Gross margin and customer churn
  • Market and acquisition source

Questions we investigate

  • Are churn and margin stable enough for the model?
  • Does observed cohort value support the estimate?
  • Are growth or expansion changing the revenue pattern?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Compare modeled value with cohort gross profit.
  • Use consistent monthly churn and margin units.
  • Replace the simple model when assumptions fail.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Finance and customer analytics leads
Monthly with periodic cohort validation.

Required data

  • Monthly revenue per paying customer
  • Gross-margin fraction and monthly customer churn
  • Cohort history and model assumption notes

Read the measure with context

Zero churn produces no finite estimate; short zero-churn samples do not establish infinite value. The model assumes stable revenue, margin, and churn, ignores discounting and expansion, and excludes acquisition cost. Monthly inputs must share the same period and customer population.
